record.paper_title: Chebyshev Sets, Klee Sets, and Chebyshev Centers with respect to Bregman Distances: Recent Results and Open Problems
record.context_brief: Necessity of supercoercivity for left D-Chebyshev convexity
record.original_question: Let X = R^n, let f: X -> [-infinity, +infinity] be a convex Legendre function, let U = int dom f, and let C be a nonempty closed subset of U. The Bregman distance induced by f is D(x, y) = f(x) - f(y) - <grad f(y), x - y> for y in U. The set C is called left D-Chebyshev when, for every y in U, the left nearest-points map P_left,C(y) = {x in C | D(x, y) = inf_{z in C} D(z, y)} is a singleton. It is known that if f is supercoercive and C is left D-Chebyshev, then C is convex. Is the supercoercivity assumption actually necessary for that convexity conclusion?

evidence.quote: Definition 1.7 (Chebyshev sets) The set C is a left Chebyshev set with respect to the Bregman distance, or simply <-D-Chebyshev, if for every y in U, <-PC(y) is a singleton.
Fact 3.1 (<- D-Chebyshev sets) (See [7, Theorem 4.7].) Suppose that f is supercoercive and that C is <-D-Chebyshev. Then C is convex.
Problem 1. Is the assumption that f be supercoercive in Fact 3.1 really essential?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X=\mathbb{R}^n$ and let $f\colon X\to[-\infty,+\infty]$ be a convex function of Legendre type (i.e., proper, lower semicontinuous, essentially smooth, and essentially strictly convex). Set $U=\operatorname{int}\operatorname{dom} f$, and define the Bregman distance induced by $f$ by
$$D(x,y)=f(x)-f(y)-\langle \nabla f(y),x-y\rangle\quad\text{for }x\in\operatorname{dom} f,\ y\in U.$$
Recall that $f$ is called supercoercive if $\lim_{\|x\|\to\infty} f(x)/\|x\|=+\infty$.

Let $C\subseteq U$ be a nonempty closed subset. For $y\in U$, define the left Bregman nearest-point map
$$P^{\leftarrow}_C(y)=\bigl\{x\in C\ :\ D(x,y)=\inf_{z\in C} D(z,y)\bigr\}.$$
The set $C$ is said to be left $D$-Chebyshev if $P^{\leftarrow}_C(y)$ is a singleton for every $y\in U$.

It is known that if $f$ is supercoercive and $C$ is left $D$-Chebyshev, then $C$ is convex.

Question: Is the supercoercivity assumption on $f$ essential for this conclusion? Equivalently, does there exist a Legendre convex function $f$ on $\mathbb{R}^n$ that is not supercoercive together with a nonempty closed left $D$-Chebyshev subset $C\subseteq U$ which fails to be convex; or can the conclusion that $C$ is convex be obtained without assuming supercoercivity?
artifact.status_search_result: Web search did not locate a published resolution of the question whether supercoercivity is essential for convexity of left D-Chebyshev sets. Subsequent work on generalized Bregman distances continues to assume supercoercivity (or related coercivity hypotheses) when deriving convexity-type conclusions, indicating the problem remains open.

status_evidence.title: Bregman distances and Chebyshev sets
status_evidence.snippet: Convexity of left D-Chebyshev sets is proved under the supercoercivity assumption on f.
status_evidence.claim: Original convexity result uses supercoercivity as a hypothesis.

status_evidence.title: The Generalized Bregman Distance
status_evidence.snippet: Sufficient conditions for convexity, coercivity, and supercoercivity are provided for the generalized Bregman distance.
status_evidence.claim: Later work still relies on supercoercivity-type conditions, without removing it in the Chebyshev setting.
